issues.legal_issue: A conviction cannot be sustained when the prosecution presents mutually contradictory sets of evidence that undermine each other’s reliability and leave no reliable evidence on which to base the conviction.
material_facts: The trial court rejected the testimony of the deceased’s sons and brother and his dying declaration, but relied on the testimony of another alleged eyewitness to convict two accused.
The High Court relied on both sets of eyewitness evidence to convict those accused of murder.

The sons’ and brother’s account of where they were when the assault began differed from the deceased’s account in his dying declaration, and the other eyewitness’s testimony indicated that they had not seen the occurrence.
The deceased’s dying declaration did not mention the other eyewitness, and the testimony of the sons and brother indicated that he had not witnessed the occurrence.
The prosecution’s own evidence thus cast doubt on the reliability of each set of eyewitness evidence, leaving no reliable and trustworthy evidence on which to sustain the convictions.
issues.conclusion: The convictions could not be sustained. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the appellants were acquitted.
issues.legal_principle: A criminal conviction must rest on reliable and trustworthy evidence. Although a conviction may be based on the testimony of a single witness if that testimony is convincing and reliable, that principle does not support a conviction when other prosecution evidence itself undermines the witness’s reliability. The Court referred to and distinguished Vadivalu Thevar v. The State of Madras, [1957] S.C.R. 981.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_against_conviction and prosecution_presented_two_sets_of_evidence and each_set_contradicted_the_other and each_set_undermined_the_other_reliability and no_reliable_evidence_remained_to_support_conviction

predicates.criminal_appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal by a person challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.prosecution_presented_two_sets_of_eviden: The prosecution relied on two distinct sets of evidence to establish the accused’s guilt.
predicates.each_set_contradicted_the_other: Each set of prosecution evidence conflicted with the account or implications of the other set.
predicates.each_set_undermined_the_other_reliabilit: The conflicts in the prosecution evidence cast doubt on the reliability of each set.
predicates.no_reliable_evidence_remained_to_support: After considering the conflicts, no reliable and trustworthy evidence remained on which to base the conviction.

issues.definition: When a person appeals a criminal conviction and the prosecution’s two conflicting sets of evidence undermine each other so that no reliable evidence supports the conviction, the accused must be acquitted.
